latest_nl_proof:
Fix integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n. Then n-r is also an integer, and 0 <= n-r <= n.

By the stated definition,
[n choose r]_q = (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}).

Since n-r is an admissible lower index as well, the same definition gives
[n choose n-r]_q = (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_{n-r} (q;q)_{n-(n-r)}) = (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_{n-r} (q;q)_r).

Now multiplication of polynomials is commutative, so
(q;q)_{n-r} (q;q)_r = (q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}.
Therefore the two right-hand sides are identical, and hence
[n choose n-r]_q = (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}) = [n choose r]_q.

Thus [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q. Since both sides are the Gaussian q-binomial coefficients defined by the given q-factorial formula, this is an identity of polynomials in q. This proves the claimed symmetry.
role_in_parent: Allows replacement of k and l by k' := min(k, n-k) and l' := min(l, n-l) without changing the quotient.
statement_nl: For all integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, if the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient is defined by [n choose r]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}), where (q;q)_m := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^i) and (q;q)_0 := 1, then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q as polynomials in q.
